# Deport Law Turkiye

> Ankara-based law office for foreigners in Turkiye: residence permits (ikamet), residence permit refusals and cancellations, deportation (removal) decisions, administrative detention in removal centres (GGM), entry bans and restriction codes such as V-87 and G-87, work permits and citizenship. Clients write on WhatsApp in their own language; the site is published in 11 languages.

Last updated: 2026-11-01. Website: https://www.deportlawturkiye.com/ · WhatsApp / phone: +90 552 524 42 26 · Location: Ankara, Turkiye.

## Key facts
- Legal framework: Law No. 6458 on Foreigners and International Protection (6458 sayılı Yabancılar ve Uluslararası Koruma Kanunu).
- A deportation (removal) decision can be challenged before the administrative court within 7 days of notification (Law No. 6458, Article 53(3)). The court decides within 15 days.
- As a rule, the person is not removed while the 7-day period runs or while the case is pending; the law makes exceptions for certain grounds, so the ground written in the decision matters.
- Administrative detention in a removal centre is challenged separately, before the criminal judgeship of peace (Law No. 6458, Article 57(6)).
- Article 54 lists the grounds for deportation; Article 55 lists persons who may not be deported.
- Residence permit applications start online on e-İkamet and are decided by the Presidency of Migration Management (Göç İdaresi Başkanlığı).

## Services
- Residence permits (ikamet): Short-term, family, student and long-term permits. Applied for and renewed, correctly the first time.
- Refusal and cancellation lawsuits: Permit refused or cancelled? We take the decision to the Administrative Court.
- Deportation appeals: You have 7 days. We file in time, and as a rule the order is not carried out while the court reviews it.
- Detention in Removal Centers (GGM): We challenge detention before the Criminal Judgeship of Peace and seek release, or a reporting duty instead.
- Lifting entry bans and codes: We work to lift restriction codes and entry bans such as V-87 and G-87, so you can return legally.
- Work permits and citizenship: Work permit and Turkish citizenship — we match your status today to your plans.

## Four steps, no guesswork
1. Message us — Write on WhatsApp in your own language. We reply fast.
2. Send your documents — Photograph the decision, your passport and your papers, and send them.
3. We plan the strategy — You get a clear answer: your deadline, your risks, your strongest route.
4. We act and represent you — We file the case and follow it through to the decision.

## Frequently asked questions
### I have just received a deportation decision. How long do I have?
The period is 7 days from the date the decision was served on you. It cannot be extended, and once it passes the decision becomes final whatever its defects. The harder questions come before that: when service was legally completed, which court is competent, and what the ground cited in your decision actually permits. Send us the decision today and we will tell you your exact last day.

### Will I be deported while the case is pending?
As a rule, filing the case suspends enforcement until the court rules. That rule has exceptions, and whether one applies to you depends on the legal ground written into your decision — for certain grounds removal may proceed while the case continues. It is the first thing we check when we open a file. Send us your decision and you will know where you stand.

### A family member is being held in a Removal Centre (GGM). What can be done?
That is administrative detention, and it is challenged separately from the deportation decision — a different application, a different authority, a different clock. Release, an alternative measure such as a reporting duty, or continued detention each depend on the ground for the detention and how long it has already run. Time matters here more than anywhere. Call us with the person's details.

### There is a restriction code or entry ban on me, for example V-87 or G-87. Can it be lifted?
It depends on which code was entered and the reason behind it. Some are removed once the underlying debt or violation is cleared; others require a lawsuit that the administration defends hard. Codes are often combined, and the combination changes the route entirely. We need to see your record before anyone can tell you honestly whether it can be lifted.

### I do not speak Turkish. Can you still help me?
Yes. Write to us on WhatsApp in your own language — Russian, Arabic, Uzbek, Persian, English and others. We explain the decision, your options and every step in the language you are comfortable with, and we represent you before the authorities and the court.

### Can I file the appeal myself, without a lawyer?
Legally, yes. In practice the court rules on the petition in front of it: the grounds you raise, the evidence you attach, the legal basis you rely on. Arguments not raised in time are usually not heard later, and a case lost on a defective petition is rarely repaired on appeal. Most of the files that reach us as emergencies started this way. Talk to us before you file, not after.

### What are my chances?
No lawyer can answer that honestly without reading your decision. The ground cited against you, your family situation in Turkiye, your health, how long you have lived here and your immigration history each change the answer — and so does the particular court. We give you an assessment once we have read the file, including when the outlook is poor.

### What documents should I send first?
Photographs of the decision you were served, your passport, and any residence or status documents you hold. That is enough for us to start reading your situation. Almost every file then needs more, and which documents matter depends on the ground cited against you. Send what you have now — the deadline keeps running while documents are collected.
